question: Kalshi settles on final corrected observations, not initial METAR reports. Does the 1.8 degF MAE target hold against NWS revisions?

initial_layer.description: frozen IEM ASOS snapshot (FM-15 METAR / FM-16 SPECI stream as first received) — the feed the engine consumes

final_layer.description: GHCN-Daily TMAX from frozen .dly archive — NWS ASOS-derived, post-QC corrected daily values

frshtt_equivalence.isd_frshtt: ISD hourly POS 133-138 + per-obs quality codes + V020/V030/C0xx QC-process markers distinguish initial vs corrected reports at hourly level; public ISD/global-hourly archives are frozen at 2025
frshtt_equivalence.operative_equivalent: GHCN-Daily .dly MFLAG/QFLAG on TMAX — the daily aggregate of the same NWS QC pipeline: QFLAG != blank = failed >=1 QC test (correction candidate), MFLAG != blank = non-standard measurement source

conventions.direction_rule: up if delta > eps, down if delta < -eps, else flat
conventions.strike_bucket: nearest whole degF, half rounds up (floor(x+0.5))

remote_probe.note: by_year feed reachable; local .dly files are the frozen audit source

caveats: GHCN-Daily TMAX is the frozen post-QC corrected proxy, not the Kalshi settlement source itself; Kalshi settles on NWS CLI/SRRS daily climate reports. The settlement cross-check quantifies the residual gap (MAE settlement vs GHCN final) — a frozen CLI/SRRS feed remains the missing settlement-truth artifact (matches the disposition in audit_ghcn_kalshi_target_equivalence.py).

Day boundaries use civil local time (zoneinfo). NWS climate-day summaries (CF6 source flag '1') run on local STANDARD time, so during DST the boundary differs by 1 h; this only matters on days whose extreme falls within that hour.
The initial layer is a frozen snapshot ending 2026-08-31 ~11Z; the final local day is truncated (caught by the coverage filter and tail adjudication, not silently mixed into headline stats).

verdict.triangle_bound_note: MAE(forecast, final) <= MAE(forecast, initial) + MAE(initial, final); the second term is this audit's revision MAE.
verdict.assessment: revision MAE 0.758 degF is within the 1.8 degF target, but by triangle inequality MAE_vs_final <= MAE_vs_initial + 0.758, so a 1.8 degF result measured on the initial stream does not automatically transfer to settlement truth; 11.0% of robust-core days revise by more than 1.8 degF (16 tail days adjudicated: {'other_tail': 3, 'snapshot_truncation': 4, 'suspect_final_value': 9}); day-over-day direction flips on revision: 11.6% of pairs — directional accuracy measured on the initial stream is benchmarked against a moving target; Kalshi strike bucket changes on 61.3% of days.

kalshi_settlement_cross_check.interpretation: If Kalshi settles against the NWS final corrected value, |settlement - final| should be materially smaller than |settlement - initial|, and rounding the initial METAR high to the strike bucket should occasionally pick the wrong contract.
